I am 67 years old. I finished primary school — five years — enough to read the numbers on fertilizer bags and keep my own accounts. I have worked these fields in Quzhou for 45 years. My son and his wife work in a factory over in Handan, so in the fields it is mostly me and my old man, though they come back to help lift garlic at harvest time. We have six mu, not a big farm but not tiny either. Every jin of seed and every yuan of electricity for the pump is real money, so I think hard before I buy anything. But I have learned this: saving 100 yuan on fertilizer and losing half a crop is the worst kind of math. I would rather put down a little too much than cry at harvest.

We grow garlic and maize on four mu — garlic goes in after National Day, comes out before June, and maize goes straight in after. The other two mu I keep in wheat for our own flour and some cash.

**Garlic (four mu):** I plant in October. Last year my own seed was small, so this year I bought 600 jin of improved seed for the four mu — that is 150 kg per mu. It cost over 1,600 yuan, but bad seed is a disaster you cannot fix later. I rotary till first to break up the soil. For fertilizer, I put down two 50-kg bags of 15-15-15 compound per mu at planting. That is about 15 kg of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium each. In March, when the garlic turns green, I topdress with one 40-kg bag of urea per mu — another 18 kg of nitrogen. I know that is a lot, but Old Wang cut back last year and his bulbs were the size of walnuts. I cover the beds with plastic film, about 4 jin per mu, to keep warmth and moisture. I irrigate four times with the well pump: once after planting, once before the freeze, once in March, and once when the bulbs swell in April. Herbicide once after planting, insecticide twice in spring. If the weather is normal I should get 2,500 jin per mu — 1,250 kg. I need that to pay for the seed.

**Maize (four mu, same land):** The day after garlic comes out in late May, I plant summer maize. No time to plough — I use no-tillage, the machine opens a slot and drops the seed. I plant Denghai 605 hybrid, one package per mu, about 1.2 kg. At sowing I put one 50-kg bag of 28-6-6 compound per mu in the row — that is about 14 kg nitrogen and 3 kg each of phosphorus and potassium. My nephew, who finished high school, says summer maize does not have time to take up extra topdressing, so I do it all at once. I irrigate twice: once after sowing if the rain does not come, and once at the big trumpet stage in July. Herbicide once, insecticide twice for the corn borer. Last year I got 1,100 jin per mu; I expect about the same, 550 kg.

**Wheat (two mu):** I plant in mid-October on the other plot. I use an improved variety, Lumai or something similar, about 30 jin per mu — 15 kg. Rotary till first. I broadcast one 50-kg bag of 18-22-5 compound per mu and one bag of ammonium bicarbonate, about 75 kg. The compound gives roughly 9 kg nitrogen and 11 kg phosphorus and 2 or 3 kg potassium; the ammonium bicarbonate adds another 13 kg nitrogen. In March I spread half a bag of urea per mu, about 9 kg nitrogen. Total nitrogen is around 22 kg per mu. I irrigate three times: winter water, jointing, and filling. Herbicide once in spring, insecticide twice, and if I see rust I spray fungicide once. I expect 1,000 jin per mu — 500 kg.

I watch my neighbors. If everyone is putting down two bags, I put down two bags. Change is risky when you are my age. I spent many years learning what works on this soil.
